summary: Every datapack, datapack generator, datapack linter, datapack test harness and datapack-focused mod in vortaforge/core is archived here and hard-disarmed: nothing under archived/ is built, merged, zipped or executed by the Gradle build or CI.

projects.name: DailyBonus
projects.reason: Abandoned by the maintainer. A datapack has no type safety: every value crossing a function call, a storage read, a scoreboard comparison or a macro expansion is an untyped string, checked by nothing at load time or run time. It has no enforced security model (dynamic command execution runs at function-permission-level with no authentication boundary), no debugging or inspection tooling, no warning surface and no error surfacing. It rated low in review, and it was bad enough that it would have been much better had it not shipped that way at all. The maintainer gave up on it after hitting real problems as a plain datapack user, without installing any client mod, and the same class of problems kept showing up in pull requests.
projects.description: DailyBonus - once-per-in-game-day login reward.
known_issues: No type safety: untyped strings everywhere (macros, storage, scoreboards), nothing validates at load or run time.
No security model: dynamic/stored-string command execution needs per-pack opt-in gates that a user cannot verify.
No debugging: no trace, breakpoint, logging or state-inspection story beyond hand-written tellraw.
No warnings: malformed references and wrong pack formats fail silently or at runtime instead of at build time.
Low review score.
The maintainer hit problems using the datapack itself, with no client mod installed.

It has no enforced security model (dynamic command execution runs at function-permission-level with no authentication boundary), no debugging or inspection tooling, no warning surface and no error surfacing. It rated low in review, and it was bad enough that it would have been much better had it not shipped that way at all. The maintainer gave up on it after hitting real problems as a plain datapack user, without installing any client mod, and the same class of problems kept showing up in pull requests.

projects.name: guigenmc (GUI datapack generator)
projects.reason: Retired with the datapack programme on 2026-11-05. A datapack has no type safety: every value crossing a function call, a storage read, a scoreboard comparison or a macro expansion is an untyped string, checked by nothing at load time or run time. It has no enforced security model, no debugging or inspection tooling, no warning surface and no error surfacing. Anything that emits .mcfunction/data/ output feeds exactly that surface, so it is archived with the programme it served rather than kept half-alive.
projects.description: Python (guigenmc) generator that turns a JSON menu spec into a Minecraft GUI datapack: emits .mcfunction files, a data/ tree and a {menu_id}_datapack.zip, plus a browser UI. Archived because its output is a datapack.
known_issues: Emits datapack output (.mcfunction + data/ + {menu_id}_datapack.zip), i.e. exactly the format the programme retired.
Generated files inherit every datapack weakness: no type safety, no security model, no debugging, no warnings.
The generator validates the menu spec but not the emitted Minecraft semantics; a wrong expansion is only visible in game.
The browser UI and the CLI are two front ends over the same emitter; keeping only one would still ship the emitter.
Still had a dedicated CI job building a wheel plus an editable install; both were removed with this move.

projects.name: build_site_data.php
projects.reason: Replaced by scripts/site/build_site_data.py. The repository builds with Gradle and tests with Python; this 172-line script was the only PHP in the tree and therefore the only reason the Pages workflow had to install a whole PHP toolchain through a third-party action (setup-php) on every run, pinned or not. Python 3 is already on the runner and is already used by the neighbouring site-validation step. The port is a behaviour-for-behaviour translation - same three attempts with linear backoff, same HTTPS-only and no-redirect rules, same fail-closed exit codes, same mod filtering, same atomic write - and it is now covered by tests, which the PHP version never was.
projects.description: PHP build-time generator for the GitHub Pages data snapshot.
known_issues: Required a PHP toolchain (setup-php) on every Pages run for one script.
Had no tests; a bad API response was only caught by reading the log.
